title: The Girl Who Wrote Down the Stories

pages.text: Esaaba’s teacher asked the class to collect a traditional story from an elder. Esaaba visited Nana Ama Serwaa in her courtyard. “Nana, may I have your permission to write down one of your stories?” she asked politely. “I will write your name as the storyteller.”
sentences: Esaaba’s teacher asked the class to collect a traditional story from an elder.
Esaaba visited Nana Ama Serwaa in her courtyard.
“Nana, may I have your permission to write down one of your stories?” she asked politely.
“I will write your name as the storyteller.”
pages.alt: Esaaba bowing slightly in polite Ghanaian greeting with her closed notebook and pencil before elderly Nana Ama Serwaa, who sits on a carved wooden stool under a courtyard mango tree.

pages.text: Nana smiled warmly. “Yes, if you listen well.” Esaaba sat quietly and listened without interrupting. Whenever she heard a word she did not know, she waited for a pause and asked, “How do you say that word, and what does it mean?”
sentences: “Yes, if you listen well.” Esaaba sat quietly and listened without interrupting.
Whenever she heard a word she did not know, she waited for a pause and asked, “How do you say that word, and what does it mean?”
pages.alt: Esaaba sitting on a woven mat with her pencil poised attentively while Nana Ama Serwaa speaks with expressive storytelling gestures.

pages.text: Esaaba wrote the story neatly in her exercise book. She kept the special Twi words Nana used, and she recorded the date and the name of their village at the top of the page.
sentences: Esaaba wrote the story neatly in her exercise book.
She kept the special Twi words Nana used, and she recorded the date and the name of their village at the top of the page.
pages.alt: Close warm scene of Esaaba writing carefully with her pencil in her open exercise book resting on her lap under the shade tree while Nana watches kindly.

pages.text: When she finished, Esaaba read every line back to Nana. “Have I written it accurately?” she asked. Nana listened closely and corrected one detail: “The chief’s drum is an atumpan talking drum.” Esaaba fixed the line right away.
sentences: When she finished, Esaaba read every line back to Nana.
“Have I written it accurately?” she asked.
Nana listened closely and corrected one detail: “The chief’s drum is an atumpan talking drum.” Esaaba fixed the line right away.
pages.alt: Esaaba holding up her open notebook and reading aloud to Nana Ama Serwaa, who points gently with one finger as she shares a helpful correction.

pages.text: At the top of the clean page, Esaaba wrote that the story was told by Nana Ama Serwaa in their village. Nana nodded with pride. “Now it is written down, and it still carries my name.”
sentences: At the top of the clean page, Esaaba wrote that the story was told by Nana Ama Serwaa in their village.
“Now it is written down, and it still carries my name.”
pages.alt: Nana Ama Serwaa smiling with pride and placing a warm hand on Esaaba’s shoulder as they look together at the finished notebook in the sunny courtyard.

pages.text: At school, Esaaba’s teacher bound everyone’s pages into a class storybook. Every story honoured the elder who had shared it. “A story is a gift,” said the teacher. “We take care of it, and we always credit the person who gave it to us.”
sentences: At school, Esaaba’s teacher bound everyone’s pages into a class storybook.
Every story honoured the elder who had shared it.
“A story is a gift,” said the teacher.
“We take care of it, and we always credit the person who gave it to us.”
pages.alt: Inside a cheerful classroom, the teacher holds open a colourful handmade class storybook for Esaaba and her smiling classmates gathered around.

activities.question: What does Esaaba do when she hears an unfamiliar word?
options: Waits politely and asks what it means

activities.question: Why does Esaaba write Nana Ama Serwaa’s name on the story?
options: To credit the elder who told it
To pretend Nana wrote the homework

items: Listen carefully and ask about unfamiliar words.
Write the story neatly with the date and village.
Read it back for checking and credit the storyteller.

activities.prompt: How would you feel if someone recorded your family’s story carefully and honoured your name?

glossary.definition: An older person in the community respected for wisdom and experience.
Clear agreement allowing someone to do something.
Speaking over someone before they have finished talking.
